An astonishingly well made game that dives into a lot of unique concepts. You don't need development experience to dive into this, or much networking experience at all. The game mostly holds your hand through the early stages until you're comfortable. 

Truly an experience worth learning, and could translate into some loose real-life skills.

Got this game because it was on sale and I was interested in it being a hacking game. I was not disappointed and would pay full price for it hands down. By no means is this game super realistic, but it is definitely intriguing and fun. It uses some real Unix commands, and has a little sense of how hacking works in the real world, however it is still a game... but it felt like so much more than that. No prior hacking/computer science experience or knowledge is needed. The game teaches you from the get go with a tutorial on the basics of how to hack nodes in the game and a few of the commands you can use. All you have to do is type "help" if you forget a command. Also you can autofill commands with the tab key which really saves you some time.

The story is very captivating. There's quite a bit of plot to uncover all while you're exploring the network of loads of IPs. It's not exactly a sandbox but you do have a bit of freedom when it comes to certain missions or hacking methods. Every step of the way this game keeps you sucked in until you finally uncover every hole you can find. Once I got to the end, my mind was blown.

I currently have 16 hours in this game. I just started the Labyrinths DLC which is already proving to be worth the buy as well. You get different background music, more GUI themes, and brand new story and collection of nodes to explore. Once I finish the DLC I am definitely going back in for another playthrough. 

Overall I would give this game a 9/10. Some parts may seem a tad bit repetitive. But the game definitely makes up for it with a great dense story, killer music, and the awesome feeling of being immersed into a world where you can become an expert hacker

This is clearly an amazing game, a near spot-on simulation, and also a headache. But my subjective experience was not fun. The Unix-like interface felt too much like work, the weird people-pleasing politics felt too much like a job, and the random timer-activated stressors, yep, felt too much like a real job. Oh, and step away from it for a few days, and you'll forget everything you need to do each step of the game. You can take notes, but the game penalizes you for that by having the notes app take up a ridiculous amount of memory. The story and the text seem okay, some of it super tropey, others of it genuinely surprising. There is some branching, but it was not enough to really carry me forward.

TLDR; A great game, a great concept, that was too much like an actual job to be fun.

Warning that it does place a (harmless) file on your computer in one mission (can't recall if this was in the DLC or not, sorry, it's been a while!) and I did have some issues getting past this - unsure if it was just that the game assumed I was using Windows, but if you're using macOS (I know, crucify me) you may have to get a little creative to finish the mission because of how Finder displays files without some custom configuration - after figuring this out I had no problem progressing despite not listening to the game's specific instructions so I don't think it was a glitch. Just a heads up!

when that beat drops and the screen gets angry, holy fuck does it feel intense. I have absolutely no clue how I managed to get so down to the wire on the endings for the main game and DLC, especially since i was not at all prepared for either. I fully thought i just... lost the game when i finished since i was so, so close. I thought i had missed something, or just finished too late, but when that email came in saying I did it, i felt such a palpable blend of excitement and legitimate relief. For all i knew, if i had failed, my game would have just deleted itself... That first time i had to change my IP, i thought if i failed, i'd just lose my save. I mean, i haven't failed at that at all, so I still don't know, but it's crazy that I've been so close to death so many times. Knees weak, arms heavy, heart racing, typo spaghetti.

More review:
The game contains a lot of really accurate and insightful tidbits about hacking, and the core plot point of the entire thing does an amazing job of getting around the inaccuracies of the shortcuts it needs to take to actually make the game work as a game. Not to mention the insane soundtrack and it's accompanying dynamic visuals. I mean, Fuck me. The soundtrack & visuals combo is just... perfect. The best among any other game I've played in this form factor.

It isn't explicitly a "hacking" game, it's more of a dedicated puzzle game with a hacking flavor. You don't need to know how to code, or even really how to use a command prompt - the game gives you all the information you need. It's focus is on figuring out how to use the tools you have to get (or modify) the files, passwords, neopet account details, etc. that you're looking for. Add onto that occasional high-octane, time-limited, music-fuckin', hacking-moments, and you get an insane, interesting puzzle game. Not to mention the compelling story. After all, what [i]would[/i] you do with a copy of [noparse]Hacknet.exe?[/noparse]

Also, if you're looking for something with more... code... go and try [url=store.steampowered.com/app/1812820/Bitburner]Bitburner[/url] (it's free) before you buy this game and complain about the lack of code
